title: Data eccentricity, asymptotics of Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and kernel PCA
abstract: We show that, up to isotropic scaling, the Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) is asymptotically isometric to Euclidean space in the large bandwidth limit. This strongly suggests that kernel-based constructions reliant on metric properties of the RKHS will yield results for Gaussian RBF kernels that similarly approach those of linear kernels for large bandwidths. The asymptotic behavior of Gaussian CKA can be understood in this light. We further consider kernel PCA, showing that Gaussian RBF eigenvalues, eigenprojections, and principal components all converge to those of classical (linear) PCA as bandwidth $σ\rightarrow \infty$. For a given data representation, both the RKHS feature embeddings and the orthogonal PCA eigenframes of the two kernel types differ asymptotically by a geometric similarity transformation, up to a residual of size $O \left (\fracρσ \right )^2$, where $ρ$ is a measure of geometric eccentricity of the representation, equal to the ratio of maximum to median pairwise distance between data examples. Experiments over a diverse collection of data sets demonstrate that $ρ$ provides a simple and reliable predictor of dataset-specific convergence behavior in the top principal directions.

E-mail: alvarez@bc.edu Abstract We show that, up to isotropic scaling, the Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) is asymptotically isometric to Euclidean space in the large bandwidth limit. This strongly suggests that kernel-based constructions reliant on metric properties of the RKHS will yield results for Gaussian RBF kernels that similarly approach those of linear kernels for large bandwidths. The asymptotic behavior of Gaussian CKA can be understood in this light. We further consider kernel PCA, showing that Gaussian RBF eigenvalues, eigenprojections, and principal components all converge to those of classical (linear) PCA as bandwidth σ → ∞ \sigma\rightarrow\infty . For a given data representation, both the RKHS feature embeddings and the orthogonal PCA eigenframes of the two kernel types differ asymptotically by a geometric similarity transformation, up to a residual of size O ​ ( ρ σ ) 2 O\left(\frac{\rho}{\sigma}\right)^{2} , where ρ \rho is a measure of geometric eccentricity of the representation, equal to the ratio of maximum to median pairwise distance between data examples. Experiments over a diverse collection of data sets demonstrate that ρ \rho provides a simple and reliable predictor of dataset-specific convergence behavior in the top principal directions. Index Terms: Nonlinear kernels, representations, Hilbert space, principal component analysis. 1 Introduction If k : ℝ d × ℝ d → ℝ k:\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R} is a positive semi-definite symmetric kernel function, the Moore-Aronszajn theorem [ 1 ] guarantees the existence of a feature map Φ : ℝ d → ℋ \Phi:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathcal{H} from the original attribute space ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} into a typically much higher-dimensional reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) ℋ \mathcal{H} , with the property that, for any data examples x i x_{i} and x j x_{j} , the value k ​ ( x i , x j ) k(x_{i},x_{j}) is the inner product ⟨ Φ ​ ( x i ) , Φ ​ ( x j ) ⟩ ℋ \langle\Phi(x_{i}),\Phi(x_{j})\rangle_{\mathcal{H}} of the feature vectors of those data examples in ℋ \mathcal{H} . Any computation that can be expressed in terms of pairwise inner products between feature vectors can therefore be carried out efficiently by the “kernel trick” (e.g., [ 2 ] ), replacing complex inner product computations in the high-dimensional RKHS by equivalent, but much simpler, evaluation of the kernel function in the original low-dimensional attribute space. The choice of kernel function is important, as it determines the RKHS feature representation. Gaussian Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels are a popular kernel type corresponding to an infinite-dimensional RKHS, and satisfy a powerful universal approximation property [ 3 ] , [ 4 ] . The latter is particularly important in light of the “representer theorem” [ 5 ] , [ 6 ] , [ 7 ] that states that kernel-based predictive models that minimize an empirical risk function are in the span of the functions k ​ ( ⋅ , y ) k(\cdot,y) for fixed y y : kernels that satisfy a universal approximation property yield hypothesis spaces that approximate any target function arbitrarily closely. Gaussian RBF kernels have been used with success in a variety of machine learning methods and applications, including support vector machines (SVM) [ 8 , 9 ] , [ 10 ] , [ 11 ] , [ 12 ] , [ 13 ] , [ 14 ] ; kernel ridge regression [ 15 ] , [ 16 ] , [ 17 ] , [ 18 ] , [ 19 ] , [ 20 ] , [ 21 ] , [ 22 ] ; centered kernel alignment (CKA) [ 23 , 24 ] , [ 25 , 26 ] , [ 27 ] , [ 28 ] , [ 29 ] , [ 30 ] , [ 31 ] ; canonical correlation analysis (CCA) [ 32 ] , [ 33 ] , [ 34 ] , [ 35 ] , [ 36 ] , [ 37 ] ; and kernel principal component analysis (kernel PCA) [ 38 ] , [ 39 ] , [ 40 ] , [ 41 ] , [ 42 ] , [ 43 ] , [ 44 ] , [ 45 ] , [ 46 ] . Contribution of the present paper We prove that, up to an isotropic scale factor, the RKHS associated with a Gaussian RBF kernel is geometrically identical to the linear kernel RKHS in the limit as the Gaussian bandwidth hyperparameter approaches infinity. We show that the metric residual is of order O ​ ( ρ / σ ) 2 O\left(\rho/\sigma\right)^{2} , where ρ \rho reflects the geometric eccentricity of the data set as measured by the ratio of maximum to median pairwise distance between data examples (Theorem 2 ). In light of our results in Theorem 2 , constructions based on the metric structure of the RKHS can be expected to yield behaviors for Gaussian RBF kernels that approach those of linear kernels for bandwidths σ ≫ ρ \sigma\gg\rho . The asymptotics of Gaussian RBF CKA [ 47 ] comprise one example of this principle. We provide an additional illustration in the present paper, by using spectral perturbation theory [ 48 ] to show that Gaussian kernel PCA is asymptotically equivalent to classical linear PCA as bandwidth σ → ∞ \sigma\rightarrow\infty (Theorem 3 ). Experiments over a range of data sets demonstrate that eccentricity, ρ \rho , reliably gauges dataset-specific convergence of the Gaussian RKHS metric structure and kernel PCA eigenvalues and eigenprojections in the top principal directions. Related work Both large- and small-bandwidth limits for support-vector machines (SVM) based on Gaussian kernels are discussed from the perspective of the dual optimization formulation of SVM in [ 49 ] . In [ 50 ] , the authors obtain spectral asymptotics results for a wide class of kernels that includes Gaussian RBF kernels. Large-bandwidth Gaussian asymptotics for Gaussian process regression are discussed in [ 51 ] . All of these works focus on uncentered kernels, however. Work involving the large-bandwidth limit for centered kernels as used in the present paper includes [ 52 ] , which discusses the related Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) for a wide class of kernels, and [ 47 ] , which deals with Gaussian RBF centered kernel alignment (CKA). The data eccentricity measure used in the present paper was introduced in [ 47 ] ; that paper showed that eccentricity is relevant to the large-bandwidth convergence of Gaussian RBF CKA, but did not uncover the root of this behavior in the geometry of the Gaussian RBF RKHS, as we do here. We are not aware of prior work that addresses the large-bandwidth asymptotics of either the Gaussian RBF RKHS metric space structure or of Gaussian RBF kernel principal components analysis (PCA), which are the main issues considered in the present paper. 2 Background 2.1 Kernel PCA Principal Components Analysis (PCA) computes the directions of maximum variance of a set of data examples, X = { x i , i = 1 ​ … ​ N } ⊂ ℝ d X=\{x_{i},\ i=1...N\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} , together with the variances in those directions, as the eigendirections and eigenvalues of the sample covariance matrix, 1 N − 1 ​ X T ​ X \frac{1}{N-1}X^{T}X (we assume that X X contains one data example per row, and that the data are centered in attribute space). The eigendirections comprise an orthogonal reference frame for ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} that aligns with the axes of linear co-variation of the data attributes. As is well known, covariance does not capture nonlinear co-variation; for example, in Fig. 1 , the sample covariance matrix is the identity, incorrectly suggesting an absence of co-variation. We do this through a direct metric analysis of the respective RKHS feature embeddings via their Gram matrices. We then show in Theorem 3 that the asymptotic geometry of the Gaussian RKHS carries over to Gaussian kernel PCA. 3.1 Isometric property of double-centering A positive semi-definite Gram matrix captures the metric structure of the corresponding Moore-Aronszajn RKHS feature embedding.
